Recent work offers useful components, but no verified exact match for a from-scratch, text-aware BERT4Rec with learned complementarity. JEPA4Rec (2025) jointly models item text and interaction sequences using bidirectional Transformers, masked-language learning, sequence–item contrastive loss, and representation prediction. Its reported setup uses cross-domain pretraining and references pretrained Longformer knowledge, so its results do not establish effectiveness under the present no-pretrained-weights constraint. Transferable idea: learn item text representations alongside recommendation rather than freeze general-purpose semantic embeddings. [JEPA4Rec](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.10512v1)

SComGNN (AAAI 2024) distinguishes complementarity from similarity: complementary products share relevance while differing in function. It models these properties through complementary-item graphs and spectral filters; this supports the conceptual distinction, but does not establish that ordinary sequential transitions identify functional complements. IBLSRec (2025) separately models user preference, intent, and long-/short-term item relationships, providing motivation for context-dependent relationships rather than static affinity. [SComGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130), [IBLSRec](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/)

Plausible experimental adaptation—not a published validated recipe: retain BERT4Rec masked-target training and appended-mask inference; jointly train a small title/description encoder from random initialization, combine its output with item-ID embeddings, and learn an asymmetric candidate interaction conditioned on the sequence and latest observed item. Optimize everything within one network/checkpoint per category. Treat inferred relationships as next-choice signals, not verified complementarity or observed user intent; use only training histories and available text, with no target text exposed at the masked input position.
